A 64 x 32 PSD written with psd-tools: a gradient background; a top row of eight 7 x 14 layers at alpha 210, blending multiply, screen, overlay, hard_light, difference, exclusion, color and luminosity; a bottom row of three adjustment layers, each masked to a 16 x 15 region (invert at 70 %, levels with a red channel record, hue / saturation on the master); a multiply in a pass-through group and a screen alone in an isolated group.
Converted by pelican-import-tools: `uv run pelican-import-tools psd-canvas fixture.psd <out> --asset-prefix project://imports/psd_blend`.
reference.png is psd-tools' composite of the layers, `PSDImage.composite(ignore_preview=True)` (psd-canvas wrote the PSD's stored preview, which psd-tools saved before the adjustment layers existed). psd-tools composites Hue / Saturation only with scipy, for its colour ranges; the reference was made with that step stubbed to "no ranges", which this PSD has none of.
soft_light is not in the PSD: psd-tools branches its D() on Cs <= 0.25 where W3C branches on Cb (the engine follows W3C). Brightness / contrast is not in it either: psd-tools needs scipy for it. modes.graph.json covers both against the CPU reference.
modes.graph.json: every blend mode the canvas names, one per 4-pixel column over the background image; every colour filter on a canvas.backdrop, masked to a 16 x 15 region (one of them blending overlay); a clip layer blending multiply; a filter on a colour layer. Its rectangles are colours masked to the region (a shape.rect's antialiased corner differs between the GPU and the CPU reference by design, CV-1). It reads the PSD's background layer and one of its masks.
Kept here: canvas.graph.json, layers/, masks/, reference.png, modes.graph.json (not the PSD, the scripts, manifest.json or canvas.report.json).
